newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nickel surcharge to rise in German stainless trade.
newsitem.headline: Nickel surcharge to rise in German stainless trade.

text.p: High nickel prices will lead to a rise in the surcharge applicable in the German stainless steel sector in May, trade and stockholders association Edelstahl handelsvereinigung (EHV) said.
It also cited firm ferrochrome prices.
Stainless steel accounts for two-thirds of nickel use.
An EHV official said surcharges in 18-10 percent chrome-nickel steel, which has a 50-60 percent share of stainless production, would rise to 560 marks a tonne in May from 460 marks in April.
"It will probably remain unchanged in June and July, but that will depend on London Metals Exchange (LME) moves," he said.
Demand for traditional flat stainless products such as sheet from car and white goods manufacturers was strong.
Traders' sales so far in 1997 had been satisfactory, EHV said.
Traders were in a modest stockbuilding phase ahead of anticipated works slowdowns in the summer and higher mill prices.
Demand for products such as bars, tubes and tool steel, which depends on seasonal swings in construction activity, had also increased.
Traders were rebuilding stocks and mill lead times for these products were lengthening.
